title: Token Runway and Fallback Matrix
content:
One-line summary:
Working sheet to estimate our short-to-medium token runway across regions & model families, and a decision matrix for automatic fallbacks when capacity/cost/SLO tradeoffs occur. This is a scratchpad intended for ops + product to iterate on regional pricing experiments and routing policies.

Context and intent:
- Problem: rapid model upgrades + variable regional infra prices are creating non-linear token COGS swings. We need a practical runway estimate (3/6/12 months) and a compact fallback matrix so the routing layer can trade off cost vs latency with predictable margin outcomes.
- Audience: Product-optimize, infra capacity planning, pricing analytics, and SRE on-call.

Key assumptions (editable cells in source sheet):
- Per-1k input+output token baseline measurements are empirically from dec/2024 workload sampler.
- Model families: LLaMA-3-7B (quantized 4-bit), LLaMA-3-13B (int8), Falcon-40B (fp16), Redwood-rlhf-33B (fp16).
- Regions: us-west, us-east, eu-west, asia-northeast. Each region has a region multiplier for GPU hourly cost (cloud list price + network egress amortization).
- QPS mix buckets: 80% short-chat (<128 tokens), 15% long-completion (512+), 5% embeddings/rerank.

Quick reference table (cells mimicking sheet columns):
Region,Model,Config,Avg seq len,Tokens per req,Tokens per 1k req,Cust price per 1k tokens (USD),Estimated infra COGS per 1k tokens (USD),Gross margin per 1k tokens (USD),Notes
us-west,LLaMA-3-7B,4-bit-quant,64,120,120000,$0.60,$0.12,$0.48,Good cost on burst instances; KV cache reduces long-tail
us-west,LLaMA-3-13B,int8,128,220,220000,$0.85,$0.22,$0.63,Better quality, moderate cost
usa-east,Falcon-40B,fp16,256,600,600000,$1.80,$0.95,$0.85,High COGS; consider routing to cheaper zone for non-low-latency
eu-west,Redwood-rlhf-33B,fp16,128,300,300000,$1.20,$0.65,$0.55,Target for enterprise SLA customers
asia-northeast,LLaMA-3-7B,4-bit-quant,64,120,120000,$0.60,$0.20,$0.40,Higher infra multiplier right now

Scenario baseline logic:
- COGS calc = (GPU amortized cost per token + networking egress + storage amortization + orchestration overhead). We model orchestration + control plane as a flat 8% surcharge on token infra.
- Price is per-1k tokens to customers (we have historical elasticity tests for +/-20%).

Runway simulations (text summary from sheet outputs):
- Conservative (low growth, stable mix): 12 months runway for current margins in us-west and eu-west for quantized families; asia-northeast hit margin erosion after month 6 due to spot price inflation.
- Growth (30% traffic yoy, mix shifts to more long completions): margin compresses ~7–12% across heavier models; without aggressive batching or forced quantization, Falcon-40B lanes become loss-making in eu and asia at month 9.
- Stress (sustained 3x peak spikes for 48 hours): routing fallbacks kick in and we observe 25–40% latency degradation but preserve margins if fallback matrix is used to downgrade to cheaper quantized variants.

Fallback decision matrix (compact rules exported from sheet):
- Trigger signals: regional spot > baseline * 1.35 for 6h, 95th pct latency > target + 100ms for 10m, margin per-1k drops below $0.30.
- For each model family, prioritized fallbacks:
  1) LLaMA-3-13B -> LLaMA-3-7B 4-bit (quality drop mild for short queries)
  2) Falcon-40B -> LLaMA-3-13B int8 -> LLaMA-3-7B quant (stepwise)
  3) Redwood-rlhf-33B -> LLaMA-3-13B (for non-enterprise routes)
- Routing policy per customer tier:
  - Free/Tier-1: aggressive fallback enabled; batch window increased to 40ms
  - Enterprise/Committed: can opt-out of fallback; use reserved capacity or negotiated SLAs

Optimization levers (prioritized from sheet scoring breakdown):
1) Region-aware model pinning: auto-route embeddings-heavy workloads to eu-west where we model lower egress cost (score +17% margin uplift).
2) Adaptive batching windows by percentiles: dynamic 5–50ms window based on queue depth; simulated uplift +9% margin on short-chat heavy flows.
3) KV prefix caching for common prompts: target top-500 prompts across customers; estimated token savings 12–18% for chat bot customers.
4) Quantization rollout: auto-quantize safe families to 4-bit with quality tests; expected 25–40% COGS savings for eligible workloads.
5) Fallback tiering in routing layer: implement N-step graceful degradation with hysteresis (avoid flip-flop).

Short technical constraints noted in sheet comments:
- Some model combos (Falcon-40B fp16) lack validated int8 kernels on our newest runtime build; rollout requires release-eng flagged tasks.
- Cross-region egress amortization line should be reconciled with infra billing team for realistic egress per request history (we currently use cloud provider average).

Concrete recommendations (actionable rows for PM/eng owners):
- Immediate (next 2 weeks): implement margin alert (per-1k token threshold) with automated Slack paging to optimize ops reaction. Owner: Liu Zhang. Ticket: JIRA-OPT-324.
- Near-term (1–2 months): build a small canary for LLaMA-3-7B 4-bit fallback for short chat templates and run A/B quality checks on 50k requests. Owner: Ethan Morales.
- Medium (2–3 months): integrate region multipliers into cost calculator used by pricing team; create automated daily scrape of cloud spot pricing and refresh sheet. Owner: Priya Kothari.
- Strategic (3–6 months): align dedicated reserved capacity pricing with Dedicated sales team to offer enterprise routing guarantees to opt-out of fallback. Owner: Marina Perez.

Open questions (for follow-up sheets/meetings):
- What fraction of committed enterprise traffic will insist on pinned model versions vs. tolerated fallback? (impact: reserved capacity sizing)
- How accurate is our current egress per-call estimate for multi-turn chat with streaming? Need sample trace recon for 10k user sessions.
- Any legal/enterprise implications of downgrading model family on PII-sensitive requests? (security/compliance check)

Data sources referenced (cells that pull external artifacts in sheet):
- workbench/api-telemetry/dec2024-sampler (internal dataset export)
- infra/costs/region-2024q4.csv (historical cloud bills)
- experiments/ab/llama3-7b-quant-quality-run1 (early quality test results)

Appendix: quick formula notes used in sheet (human readable)
- COGS_per_1k = (GPU_hourly_effective / tokens_per_hour) * 1000 + egress_per_req * requests_per_1k + storage_amort_per_1k + orchestration_pct*sum(previous)
- margin_per_1k = price_per_1k - COGS_per_1k

Next steps to finalize sheet into product playbook:
- Reconcile infra egress numbers with billing (finance) and push a corrected multiplier into the model by 2025-03-15.
- Run the LLaMA-3-7B fallback canary across us-west and eu-west for 2 weeks and produce a quality regression report.
- Update the fallback matrix to expose weighting fields for query-type so routing can avoid quality-sensitive downgrades for long completion flows.

Notes to self (scratch):
- Add small pivot showing token mix sensitivity: vary short-chat % from 60–90 and see margin cliff.
- Build a quick viz: scatter of margin_per_1k vs latency_p95 colored by region.

Revision log (manual):
- 2025-02-11 initial draft (Priya)
- 2025-02-25 added simulation outputs and fallback matrix (Ethan)
- 2025-03-03 updated region multipliers and recommended owners (Priya)

End of sheet scratchpad.
